name: FluidGlass-TS-TW

frames.best_why: A faint circular glass edge is visible over the left photo with the image bending inside it, showing the lens at work.

tagline: A glass lens drifts with the pointer and bends the photos behind it.
summary: A violet full-screen scene shows two large photos and a bold wordmark. A round glass disc follows the cursor, refracting and warping whatever passes beneath it.
appearance: A vivid violet backdrop holds a tall photo of dark rocks and surf on the left and a city skyline on the right, with large white lettering across the middle. A faint circular glass disc hovers over the scene.
behaviour: The glass disc trails the pointer with a soft delay, bending and shifting the image under it with faint colour fringes at the rim. When the pointer stops, the scene settles back to flat.
demo_content: A wave-and-rock photo, a city skyline photo, and the wordmark 'React Bits' on a violet background.
search_phrases: glass lens that follows the cursor
magnifying bubble over a hero image
purple hero with a floating lens
interactive glass magnifier for a landing page
use_when: A bold hero wants an eye-catching glass magnifier that tracks the pointer.
avoid_when: It needs WebGL and a sized parent, and touch users never get the lens effect.
customise: Mode (lens, bar or cube) and glass settings such as scale, refraction, thickness and chromatic aberration are props; the photos and wordmark are hardcoded.
weight_why: A three.js canvas renders every frame with a transmission material and an offscreen buffer.

a11y.note: The scene lives entirely in a WebGL canvas with no text alternative, and the lens ignores reduced-motion settings.

issues: The lens is barely visible over the busy photos, reading as a faint dark ring.
The photos and the 'React Bits' wordmark are hardcoded, so every page shows the same scene.
polish_why: Convincing glass refraction on a bold violet scene; the lens edge is hard to spot on busy photos.
